findings.issue: Every resolver's catch-all converts any fetch failure into null, so a transient API error (500, timeout) renders the Not-found page with a 404 status; failures in secondary fetches reject the resolver with no withNavigationErrorHandler configured, which surfaces as an SSR 500 or a dead client navigation.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish 404 from other errors (check the HttpErrorResponse status) and add withNavigationErrorHandler to provideRouter for a graceful fallback.

findings.issue: A single 400-line module owns all six route resolvers plus every API resource and page-data interface, mixing the data shapes of five features in one file — a merge hotspot and a leaky boundary.
findings.suggestion: Split per feature (pokemon-data.ts, move-data.ts, type-data.ts, …) with a small shared home for cross-feature helpers like typeRef and pokemonRefsToCards.

findings.issue: The search debounce timer is never cleared on destroy; navigating away from the home page within ~200 ms of typing fires router.navigate('/') afterwards, hijacking the navigation.
findings.suggestion: Register a cleanup with inject(DestroyRef) or use toObservable + takeUntilDestroyed for the debounced search.

findings.issue: value="{{ q() }}" re-applies the (trimmed) URL value after the debounced navigation, clobbering characters typed during the debounce window and resetting the cursor.
findings.suggestion: Drop the value binding after hydration or sync the input imperatively only when the query param changes externally (e.g. via linkedSignal/patch or an effect guarded by document.activeElement).

findings.issue: The same Title-setting effect is duplicated in four page components (pokemon, move, ability, type) while the router offers a first-class mechanism for it.
findings.suggestion: Use the route `title` property (static or a ResolveFn<string>) or a custom TitleStrategy, and delete the four copies.

findings.issue: The response cache is a module-level Map: hidden global state, unbounded, untestable and impossible to reset between requests or tests despite being shared by every SSR request in the process.
findings.suggestion: Move the cache into the PokeApi service (or an injectable Cache provider) so it can be scoped, inspected and replaced in tests; consider a max-size or TTL.

findings.issue: A presentational card-list component injects the PokeApi data service solely to build sprite URLs, coupling rendering to the data layer and making the component awkward to reuse or test.
findings.suggestion: Include the sprite URL in PokemonCardData (it already carries id/name) or expose a small pure spriteUrl(id) helper/pipe.

findings.issue: The server defaults to port 4000 while the spec documents 3000 as the default, and untouched CLI scaffold comments ('Example Express Rest API endpoints…') remain in the production server file.
findings.suggestion: Default to process.env['PORT'] || 3000 and strip the scaffold comment block.

findings.issue: @angular/forms is a declared dependency but no forms module or API is used anywhere (the app uses native form elements with event handlers).
findings.suggestion: Remove the dependency to keep the install lean.

findings.issue: Vitest and a test builder are fully configured but the app contains zero unit tests, and the pure helpers here (humanize, latestEnglishFlavor, dexNumber, pokemonRefsToCards, compareValues) are exactly the kind of spec-prone logic a team regression suite wants.
findings.suggestion: Add a few focused unit specs for util.ts and the catalog/card-mapping logic so future edits to display rules are protected.

summary: A genuinely idiomatic Angular 22 app: resolvers with component input binding, signals throughout, proper SSR route configuration, TransferState and real 404s — it reads like the framework's own examples. The main merge blockers are hygiene, not architecture: resolvers that turn any API failure into a 404, one 400-line god data module, and a handful of small leaks (debounce timer, hidden module-level cache, duplicated title effects). I'd approve after one pass of contained fixes.
